title: Finite-open constant generators under extensions and retracts
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $B$ a finite field. In the category of sheaves of $B_S$-modules on the ordinary small etale site, every constructible sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] belongs to the smallest full subcategory closed under isomorphisms, finite direct sums, extensions and direct summands and containing all sheaves
$$\pi_*k_!B_W,$$
where $\pi:S'\to S$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $S'$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $k:W\hookrightarrow S'$ is a nonempty open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Here $k_!$ is ordinary etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $\pi_*$ is ordinary etale direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Membership in this smallest subcategory means that each individual constructible sheaf is obtained by finitely many such operations; no closure under arbitrary subobjects or quotients is asserted.

source.place: XIII 3.7.2, finite-field form of the constructible-sheaf devissage (the prime-field case extends along the finite separable coefficient-field extension)

proof.text: Fix $B$ and $S$, and denote the subcategory in the statement by $\mathcal C_S$. If $h:Z\to S$ is finite, its direct image is additive and exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; this assertion for $B$-modules follows on forgetting scalars, since kernels and cokernels of module maps are formed with their induced scalar actions. It therefore preserves finite sums, extensions and retract diagrams. On generators, the section formula in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] identifies $h_*(q_*k_!B)=(hq)_*k_!B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] says $hq$ is finite. Hence $h_*$ takes any finite construction from the specified generators over $Z$ to such a construction over $S$.

source.place: Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero; finite compositions: morphisms.tex Tag 01WK, lemma-composition-finite

proof.text: For each closed subset $T\subseteq |S|$, give $T$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $i_T:T_{\rm red}\to S$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Prove by induction on proper closed subsets that $i_{T*}G\in\mathcal C_S$ for every constructible $B$-module sheaf $G$ on $T_{\rm red}$. The induction is legitimate by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]: a nonempty collection of failures has a minimal closed support. The empty support gives the zero sheaf, the empty finite sum. Closed subschemes here are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is enough to establish the induction step for nonempty $T$.

source.place: Noetherian induction on closed supports; topology.tex Tag 0052 and properties.tex Tag 01OZ

proof.text: Write $R=T_{\rm red}$. Its finitely many irreducible components are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] supplies a finite locally closed partition adapted to $G$, with reduced strata allowed. For each component, its generic point lies in one stratum, and that locally closed stratum contains a nonempty open of the component: its closed part contains the generic point and hence the whole component. Remove all other components and shrink to an affine open in this stratum. This yields pairwise disjoint nonempty affine opens $U_b\subseteq R$, one in each component, on each of which $G$ is finite locally constant as a $B$-module. Their union is dense. The reduced induced closed component $C_b\subseteq R$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] and is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]; $U_b$ is an open subscheme of $C_b$.

source.place: XIII 3.7.2, constructible-sheaf reduction, with topology.tex Tag 0052, lemma-Noetherian, and the defining finite stratification

proof.text: Let $\ell=\operatorname{char}B$, a prime, and apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-lisse-finite-etale-filtration] with $X=U_b$, $\Lambda=B$, $n=1$ and $F=G|_{U_b}$. All hypotheses hold: $U_b$ is affine Noetherian, $B$ is finite, the fibres of $F$ are finite and $\ell F=0$. We obtain a finite etale surjection $g_b:T_b\to U_b$ of constant degree $d_b\ge1$ prime to $\ell$. The pullback $g_b^{-1}F$ has, on each of finitely many open-and-closed pieces of $T_b$, a finite filtration by $B$-submodule sheaves with constant finite $B$-module quotients.

source.place: Tags 0GJ0, lemma-pullback-filtered-modules (finite-ring version supplied by the cited node), and 0DV5, lemma-locally-constant-on-connected

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-finite-etale-integral-models-after-shrinking] to $C_b$, $U_b$ and $g_b$. Replace $U_b$ by the resulting nonempty affine open $W_b$ and restrict the cover to $v_b:V_b\to W_b$. Keep these shrunken opens throughout the rest of the induction step. Each $W_b$ still meets the generic point of its component, so $W=\coprod_bW_b$ is open dense in $R$. The cited node gives a finite disjoint family of integral $Y_{ba}\to C_b$ with $V_b=\coprod_a(Y_{ba}\times_{C_b}W_b)$. Composing with the closed immersion $C_b\to R$ gives finite maps $q_{ba}:Y_{ba}\to R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. The square for $q_b:\coprod_aY_{ba}\to R$ and $W_b\hookrightarrow R$ is cartesian, with upper open $V_b$.

source.place: Integral finite models after shrinking, from more-morphisms.tex Tag 05K0

proof.text: Restriction to $V_b$ preserves the finite filtrations of Step 4 by the exact constant-coefficient inverse image [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Intersect each filtration piece with each integral open component $V_{ba}\subseteq V_b$. An irreducible space cannot meet two disjoint nonempty clopen pieces, so each $V_{ba}$ lies in one of the original clopen pieces. Its successive quotients are therefore constant finite-dimensional $B$-vector spaces. Choosing a basis identifies each such quotient with a finite sum of $B_{V_{ba}}$; a basis flag refines it into rank-one constant quotients. The elementary finite-dimensional argument uses only that $B$ is a field.

source.place: Restriction of the finite-ring filtration of Tag 0GJ0 to integral opens; constant-coefficient inverse image

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-degree], restriction followed by trace for $v_b$ is $d_b\,\mathrm{id}_F$ on $W_b$, with the same degree $d_b$: every geometric fibre is a fibre of the original $g_b$. Naturality of trace in [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace] applied to each scalar endomorphism $m_c$ ($c\in B$) shows $\operatorname{tr}\,v_*v^{-1}(m_c)=m_c\operatorname{tr}$, so trace is $B$-linear. The unit is also $B$-linear. As $\ell\nmid d_b$, $d_b^{-1}\operatorname{tr}$ is a retraction of $F\to v_{b*}v_b^{-1}F$ in $B$-module sheaves. Thus $F$ is a retract of the latter, with no use of closure under quotients or subobjects.

source.place: Tag 03SH, section-trace-method, restriction followed by trace and etale-local sum formula

proof.text: Put $j_b:W_b\hookrightarrow R$ and $k_b:V_b\hookrightarrow Y_b=\coprod_aY_{ba}$. The finite-open isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-extension-zero] gives $j_{b!}v_{b*}H\cong q_{b*}k_{b!}H$. Although stated for abelian sheaves, it is $B$-linear on module sheaves: naturality for every multiplication $m_c$ makes the comparison commute with each constant scalar, and the induced scalar actions are sheaf-local. Exactness of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] sends the filtrations of Step 6 to filtrations of $q_{b*}k_{b!}v_b^{-1}F$. Disjoint components give finite direct sums (sections are finite products, equal to finite sums of modules), and every successive quotient is a finite sum of $q_{ba*}k_{ba!}B_{V_{ba}}$. Each $Y_{ba}$ is integral and $V_{ba}$ nonempty open, so these are exactly allowed generators over $R$.

source.place: Tag 0GJ1, lemma-compatible-shriek-push-finite; exact extension by zero and Tag 03QP

proof.text: Step 8 constructs $j_{b!}v_{b*}v_b^{-1}F$ by finitely many sums and extensions from generators. Applying the additive functor $j_{b!}$ to the split pair of Step 7 exhibits $j_{b!}F$ as a retract. Step 1, applied to the finite closed immersion $i_T$, therefore places $i_{T*}j_{b!}F$ in $\mathcal C_S$. Finite sums over $b$ place $i_{T*}j_!j^{-1}G$ in $\mathcal C_S$, where $j:W\hookrightarrow R$; the identification with the sum follows from the extension-by-zero stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and the disjointness of the $W_b$, or directly from its direct-sum presheaf construction.

source.place: XIII 3.7.2, closure under extensions and direct factors, now with the explicit finite constructions

proof.text: Let $a:Z\hookrightarrow R$ be the reduced closed complement of $W$. The ordinary open-closed triangle [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] applied to $G[0]$ gives, on degree-zero cohomology, the short exact sequence $0\to j_!j^{-1}G\to G\to a_*a^{-1}G\to0$, since all three functors in that triangle are exact sheaf functors. The sheaf $a^{-1}G$ is constructible: [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] gives its finite underlying constructible stratification, and the module-local trivializations are obtained by pulling back the defining trivializations of $G$ using [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. The closed subset $|Z|$ is proper in $T$ since $W$ is dense nonempty. The induction hypothesis gives $(i_Ta)_*a^{-1}G\in\mathcal C_S$. Apply the exact $i_{T*}$ to this sequence; its left term is in $\mathcal C_S$ by Step 9 and its right term by induction, hence its middle term $i_{T*}G$ is in $\mathcal C_S$.

source.place: Open-closed localization, and Tag 03QP for exact closed pushforward; the sheaf sequence is the degree-zero sequence of the cited triangle

proof.text: Finally let $r:S_{\rm red}\to S$ be the reduction. It is a finite closed immersion and a universal homeomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. The equivalence [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] gives the adjunction isomorphism $F\cong r_*r^{-1}F$. This is an isomorphism of $B$-modules: the inverse-image equivalence transports addition and each scalar map, and its unit is natural in those maps. The pullback is constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-set-pullback] and the same defining module trivializations as in Step 10. The induction result with $T=|S|$ puts $r_*r^{-1}F$ in $\mathcal C_S$. Thus $F$ belongs to $\mathcal C_S$. The induction uses proper closed supports and finitely many covers, filtration steps and components at each step; equivalently the minimal-counterexample proof establishes membership in the closure defined by finite constructions. No infinite operation is used.

source.place: Tag 03SI, proposition-topological-invariance, and reduced induced closed structures

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q60-2b64aa647 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 11 steps, the new node and every cited statement, and checked the item against ILO XIII 3.7.2 (p. 203). The source cites SGA 5 I 3.1.2 for this reduction. The split does not use SGA anywhere: it proves the reduction by Noetherian induction on reduced closed supports, the existing finite-ring Sylow filtration node, the degree-trace retraction (W_b is irreducible, so connected, and d is prime to ell), the finite-open isomorphism (Stacks 0GJ1) on a square that is cartesian by the new node's full-preimage clause, and the degree-zero open-closed sequence, with reduction via 03SI. The statement is unchanged and matches its citer, lem-per-gabber-open-immersion-sheaf-finiteness Step 8. Hypotheses checked: affine Noetherian and ell F=0 in Step 4; |Z| a proper subset of T in Step 10; T_red = S_red in Step 11. New node lem-per-finite-etale-integral-models-after-shrinking: it is true. My proof: T is reduced and all its components lie over the generic point (flatness); shrinking separates them; Stacks 05K0 gives a finite model; take the reduced closure; T_i is closed in Y_W because it is finite over W, and dense, so T_i = Y_W. Tested on a field base and on a nodal cubic with a crosswise double cover. B1-B9 hold. It is strictly smaller than the item and not a duplicate: only thm-pqf-zmt-factorization (no integral components) and curve-specific nodes come close. No cycle (719-node closure). The tool_uses inside split_report list all 17 off-unit generic tools, and I accept them. Advisory: Step 4 does not cite a node for 'affine open of a Noetherian scheme has Noetherian ring' (Stacks 01OT), a standard fact. No fixes.
